questions.question: Which of the following is NOT located in the Andaman group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minicoy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Minicoy** is part of the **Lakshadweep group of islands**, not the Andaman group.
 
• The **Andaman Islands** are located in the Bay of Bengal, while the **Lakshadweep Islands** are in the Arabian Sea.
 
• Minicoy is known for its distinctive culture and is the southernmost island of the Lakshadweep group.
 
• Other islands mentioned in the question—Havelock, Neil, and Barren—are part of the Andaman archipelago.
 
• The Andaman and Lakshadweep groups are geographically and administratively distinct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman Islands:**

 
 
• Located in the Bay of Bengal, the Andaman Islands are part of the union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• Famous islands include Havelock Island (now Swaraj Dweep) and Neil Island (now Shaheed Dweep).
 
• Home to the **Indigenous Andamanese tribes** and rich in biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:**
 
 
• Located in the Arabian Sea, the Lakshadweep Islands are India's smallest union territory.
 
• Minicoy is the second-largest island in this group and culturally distinct due to its Maldivian influences.
 
• The islands are known for their coral atolls and lagoons.
 
 
 
• **Barren Island:**
 
 
• Barren Island, located in the Andaman group, is home to India's only active volcano.
 
• It lies approximately 135 km northeast of Port Blair.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distinction:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Lakshadweep islands are separated by vast distances and are located in different seas.
 
• Andaman Islands are closer to Myanmar, whereas Lakshadweep Islands are closer to the Malabar Coast of India.

questions.question: Bholanath Singh was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamar Revolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bholanath Singh** was a prominent leader of the **Tamar Revolt**, which took place in the region of **Jharkhand**.
 
• The Tamar Revolt occurred during the early 19th century, specifically in the **year 1789** against the oppressive practices of landlords and the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt was largely driven by tribal communities, including the **Munda tribes**, who resisted exploitative policies and forced taxation.
 
• Bholanath Singh played a crucial role in organizing the tribal groups and leading them in their fight against exploitation and injustice.
 
• The Tamar Revolt was one of the early tribal revolts in India, showcasing the resistance of indigenous communities against colonial rule and feudal oppression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Revolts in India:**

 
 
• Tribal revolts like the **Santhal Revolt (1855-56)**, the **Kol Revolt (1831)**, and the **Munda Revolt (1899-1900)** were significant uprisings against colonial exploitation and local feudal systems.
 
• These revolts were characterized by the resistance of tribal communities against policies that disrupted their traditional ways of life.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Colonial Policies:**
 
 
• The British introduced land revenue policies that marginalized tribal communities and forced them into bonded labor and economic exploitation.
 
• These policies led to widespread resentment among tribal groups, culminating in revolts like the Tamar Revolt.
 
 
 
• **Leadership in Tribal Movements:**
 
 
• Tribal leaders like Bholanath Singh and others such as **Birsa Munda** played a crucial role in organizing resistance against colonial and feudal systems.
 
• Their leadership was instrumental in galvanizing tribal communities to fight for their rights and preserve their cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Tribal Resistance:**
 
 
• Tribal uprisings like the Tamar Revolt are considered important milestones in the history of India's fight against colonial oppression.
 
• They laid the foundation for later movements that emphasized social justice and the rights of indigenous communities.

questions.question: The award (decision) made by the Lok Adalats is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and is final and binding on all parties because:

options.text: An appeal can be filed in the Supreme Court
A review petition can be filed
An appeal can be filed in the High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No appeal is permissible**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The award or decision of a Lok Adalat is deemed as equivalent to a decree of a civil court under the provisions of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• Once a settlement is reached in Lok Adalat, it is binding on all parties and no appeal is permissible to challenge the decision.
 
• Lok Adalat promotes voluntary conciliation and consensus-based dispute resolution, ensuring quicker and cost-effective justice.
 
• It is designed to avoid prolonged litigation by resolving disputes amicably without the need for a formal trial.
 
• The finality of the award is emphasized to maintain the efficiency and credibility of Lok Adalats as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat:**

 
 
• Lok Adalat (People's Court) is a statutory body under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• It is organized to provide free legal aid and resolve disputes through conciliation and compromise.
 
• Cases like civil disputes, matrimonial disputes, labor disputes, and compoundable criminal cases are usually resolved by Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:**
 
 
• This Act provides the framework for organizing Lok Adalats and ensuring free legal aid to economically weaker sections.
 
• It establishes State and District Legal Services Authorities to oversee the implementation of legal aid and Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Lok Adalat:**
 
 
• Eliminates the lengthy process of litigation and provides speedy justice.
 
• Reduces the burden on regular courts and saves resources.
 
• Fosters mutual understanding and peace among disputing parties.
 
 
 
• **Binding Nature of Awards:**
 
 
• The award is final and cannot be appealed, ensuring quick and decisive resolution of disputes.
 
• Parties must voluntarily agree to the settlement before the award is passed.

questions.question: Which shortcut key combination is used to insert a hyperlink in MS PowerPoint 365?

• A hyperlink is a reference or link that directs users to another location, such as a webpage, document, or slide.
 
• Hyperlinks can be embedded in text, images, or other objects in presentations and documents.
 
 
 
• **Interactive Presentations:**
 
 
• Hyperlinks in PowerPoint are used to create interactive slides that allow users to navigate between slides or external resources.
 
• This is especially useful for business, educational, and marketing presentations.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in MS Office:**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts enhance productivity by allowing users to perform tasks quickly without using the mouse.
 
• Examples include **Ctrl + C** for copy, **Ctrl + V** for paste, and **Ctrl + S** for save.
 
 
 
• **Universal Shortcut:**
 
 
• The **Ctrl + K** shortcut is available across all major versions of Microsoft Office, including Office 365.
 
• It can be used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for hyperlink insertion.

questions.question: In which type of musical instruments is sound produced by blowing air into a hollow column?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sushira Vadya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sushira Vadya** refers to wind instruments where sound is produced by blowing air into a hollow column.
 
• Common examples of Sushira Vadya include the flute, shehnai, and harmonium.
 
• The vibration of air within the hollow tube creates sound, and the pitch can be varied by changing the length of the air column.
 
• These instruments are categorized under the ancient Indian classification of musical instruments based on how sound is produced.
 
• Sushira Vadya is distinct from other categories like Tata Vadya (string instruments) or Avanaddha Vadya (percussion instruments).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Classification of Indian Musical Instruments:**

 
 
• Indian instruments are traditionally classified into four types: Tata Vadya (string instruments), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion instruments), Sushira Vadya (wind instruments), and Ghana Vadya (solid instruments).
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Sound Production:**
 
 
• In Sushira Vadya, air vibrations caused by blowing into the instrument generate sound waves within the hollow column.
 
• The frequency of these waves determines the pitch, which can be manipulated using finger holes or valves.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sushira Vadya:**
 
 
• Traditional instruments: Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram.
 
• Modern instruments: Clarinet, Saxophone.
 
 
 
• **Role in Indian Music:**
 
 
• Sushira Vadya plays a vital role in both classical and folk music traditions.
 
• These instruments are often used for melody and accompaniment.

questions.question: Where can people of Indian origin living abroad apply for Indian citizenship under Article 8?

options.text: Indian Embassy at their country of living

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Embassy at their country of living**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 8 of the Constitution of India, persons of Indian origin residing outside the country can apply for Indian citizenship at the **Indian Embassy or Consulate in their country of residence**.
 
• Article 8 specifically provides for Indian citizenship to those who have Indian origin but are **ordinarily residing outside India**.
 
• The individual must be registered as a citizen of India by the diplomatic or consular representative of India in that country.
 
• The process involves verification of the applicant's Indian origin and other supporting documentation by the concerned diplomatic mission.
 
• This provision is part of the broader framework of the Indian Constitution's citizenship laws, which include Articles 5 to 11.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• These articles deal with the acquisition and termination of citizenship in India.
 
• They provide the constitutional framework for Indian citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution in 1950.
 
• Article 8 is particularly relevant for individuals of Indian origin living abroad.
 
 
 
• **Indian Citizenship Act, 1955:**
 
 
• This act governs the acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship after the Constitution came into effect.
 
• It provides various modes for acquiring citizenship, such as birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
 
 
• **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI):**
 
 
• OCI is a scheme launched by the Government of India to facilitate individuals of Indian origin who do not qualify for Indian citizenship but want to maintain a connection with India.
 
• OCI does not grant full citizenship but provides certain privileges like visa-free travel and property ownership in India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Diaspora:**
 
 
• The Indian diaspora is one of the largest in the world, with millions of individuals of Indian origin living in various countries.
 
• They play a significant role in fostering economic, cultural, and political ties between India and their countries of residence.

questions.question: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve spans which of the following groups of Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is India's first biosphere reserve, established in **1986**.
 
• It spans across three Indian states: **Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka**.
 
• The reserve covers an area of approximately **5,520 square kilometers**.
 
• It is part of the **Western Ghats**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its rich biodiversity.
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is home to several endemic species, including the **Nilgiri Tahr** and the **Lion-tailed Macaque**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosphere Reserve:**

 
 
• A biosphere reserve is an area designated to protect biodiversity and promote sustainable development.
 
• It comprises three zones: the core area (protected region), buffer zone (activities promoting conservation), and transition area (sustainable resource use).
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• It is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its unique ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve hosts over **3,000 species of flowering plants** and a variety of mammals, birds, reptiles, and insects.
 
• Endangered species like the **Tiger**, **Elephant**, and **Nilgiri Langur** are found here.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Program:**
 
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is part of UNESCO’s **Man and Biosphere (MAB) Program**, which promotes conservation and sustainable development.
 
• It aims to balance environmental conservation with human activity.

questions.question: In which of the following countries did the United Nations Biodiversity Convention 2024 (COP16) conclude in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colombia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP16) is scheduled to be held in **Colombia** in February 2025.
 
• Colombia, known for its rich biodiversity, was chosen to host this crucial event, emphasizing its role in global biodiversity conservation.
 
• The conference is a part of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), which aims to promote sustainable development and address global biodiversity loss.
 
• Previous COPs under the CBD have focused on the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which sets targets for biodiversity protection until 2030.
 
• The event will bring together governments, scientists, and stakeholders to discuss and implement strategies for biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**

 
 
• The CBD is an international treaty adopted at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
 
• Its primary objectives include the conservation of biodiversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
 
• It has been ratified by 196 parties, making it a near-universal environmental agreement.
 
 
 
• **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework:**
 
 
• Adopted during COP15 in 2022, this framework sets 23 global targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.
 
• Key targets include protecting 30% of the planet's land and oceans and restoring degraded ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots:**
 
 
• Colombia is one of the world's most biodiverse countries, hosting a significant portion of the Amazon rainforest, Andes mountain range, and Orinoco plains.
 
• It is home to 10% of the planet’s species, making it a critical location for global biodiversity conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Previous COP Locations:**
 
 
• COP15 was held in two parts: Kunming, China (2021), and Montreal, Canada (2022).
 
• COP14 was hosted in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt, in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Role of COP16:**
 
 
• COP16 will review the progress made under the Kunming-Montreal framework and address emerging issues in biodiversity conservation.
 
• It will also provide a platform for nations to discuss financing mechanisms and partnerships for achieving biodiversity targets.

questions.question: What major tax reform was introduced by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax (GST)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the **101st Amendment Act, 2016**.
 
• It was implemented on **July 1, 2017**, replacing multiple indirect taxes like service tax, VAT, and excise duty.
 
• GST is a **destination-based tax**, meaning it is levied at the point of consumption rather than the point of origin.
 
• The tax structure includes four main slabs: **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**, depending on the type of goods and services.
 
• GST is governed by a dual structure, where both the Central Government (CGST) and State Governments (SGST) collect taxes on intra-state transactions, while inter-state transactions attract Integrated GST (IGST).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Input Tax Credit (ITC):**

 
 
• Under GST, businesses can claim credit for taxes paid on purchases as a set-off against taxes payable on sales.
 
• This eliminates the cascading effect of taxes, making the tax system more efficient.
 
 
 
• **GST Council:**
 
 
• The GST Council is a constitutional body chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
 
• It consists of representatives from both the Central and State Governments to decide GST rates, policies, and reforms.
 
 
 
• **Types of GST:**
 
 
• **CGST:** Central Goods and Services Tax, levied by the central government.
 
• **SGST:** State Goods and Services Tax, levied by state governments.
 
• **IGST:** Integrated Goods and Services Tax, applicable on inter-state transactions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GST:**
 
 
• GST has simplified the tax structure in India by consolidating multiple indirect taxes.
 
• It has improved tax compliance and brought transparency to the taxation system.
 
• It has boosted India's ease of doing business rankings by streamlining tax processes for businesses.

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula of pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**[ML⁻¹T⁻²]**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **force** applied per unit **area**.
 
• Mathematically, **Pressure = Force / Area**.
 
• **Force** has the dimensional formula **[MLT⁻²]**, where M = mass, L = length, T = time.
 
• **Area** has the dimensional formula **[L2]**.
 
• Dividing force by area gives **[MLT⁻²] / [L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²]**, which is the dimensional formula of pressure.
 
• **Applications:** Pressure is used in fields like **fluid mechanics, hydraulics, meteorology, and engineering design**.
 
• **Examples:** Atmospheric pressure, blood pressure, and pressure in hydraulic lifts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **[ML⁻²T⁻²]**__: This dimensional formula corresponds to **surface tension**.

 __
 
• **Surface tension** represents force per unit **length** along the surface of a liquid.
 
• Common applications include **capillary action, formation of droplets, and liquid interfaces in engineering.**
 
 
 
• **[ML²T⁻²]**__: This represents **moment of force or torque**.
 __
 
• It is calculated as **Force × Distance** from the pivot.
 
• Used in applications such as **lever systems, mechanical rotation, and structural analysis.**
 
 
 
• **[MLT⁻²]**__: This is the dimensional formula for force itself.
 
 
• **Force** acts on objects to produce **acceleration**.
 
• Applications include **mechanics, dynamics, and structural design calculations.**

questions.question: The mention of DNA as a long polymer of deoxyribonucleotides implies which structural characteristic?

options.text: It is composed of a sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.
Each nucleotide is linked by hydrogen bonds in a parallel fashion.
The molecule consists of multiple independent short chains.
The sequence is circular and self-replicating.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is composed of a sugar-phosphate backbone and nitrogenous bases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is a long polymer composed of repeating units called **deoxyribonucleotides**, which form the basic structural framework.
 
• Each nucleotide in DNA consists of three components: a **deoxyribose sugar**, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base.
 
• The sugar-phosphate backbone forms the structural framework, while the nitrogenous bases project inward, forming complementary base pairs.
 
• The nitrogenous bases include **adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G)**, which pair specifically (A with T and C with G) through hydrogen bonding.
 
• This arrangement results in the characteristic **double-helix structure** of DNA, with the sugar-phosphate backbone on the outside and base pairs on the inside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleotides:** The building blocks of DNA, composed of a nitrogenous base, a deoxyribose sugar, and a phosphate group.
 
• **Complementary Base Pairing:** Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, while cytosine pairs with guanine through three hydrogen bonds, ensuring the stability of the double helix.
 
• **Sugar-Phosphate Backbone:** This backbone provides structural integrity and is formed through phosphodiester bonds between the 5' phosphate group of one nucleotide and the 3' hydroxyl group of the adjacent nucleotide.
 
• **Double-Helix Model:** Proposed by Watson and Crick in 1953, the DNA double helix consists of two antiparallel strands twisted around each other.
 
• **Central Dogma of Molecular Biology:** DNA serves as the template for RNA synthesis (transcription), which in turn guides protein synthesis (translation), highlighting its critical role in genetic information storage and expression.

questions.question: Which aspect of life is explored under the theme of akam in Sangam literary works?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Love**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• **Akam** in Sangam literature refers to the inner, personal, and emotional aspects of life, especially focusing on the theme of **love**.
 
• Sangam poetry categorizes emotions and situations of love into distinct landscapes or **‘tinai’**, which are symbolic of specific moods and settings.
 
• The Akam theme encompasses the intimate experiences of individuals, such as courtship, marriage, and separation.
 
• Unlike themes like war or politics, Akam focuses on the **domestic and emotional realm**, representing the personal lives of individuals.
 
• The concept of Akam is complemented by **Puram**, which deals with external aspects like war, heroism, and public life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature:** It is a body of classical Tamil literature created between 300 BCE and 300 CE, known for its rich depiction of Tamil culture, society, and emotions.
 
• **Five Landscapes of Akam:** The emotions of love are categorized into five landscapes—Kurinji (mountains), Mullai (forests), Marutham (plains), Neythal (seashore), and Palai (deserts), each representing a specific mood or phase of love.
 
• **Puram vs Akam:** While Akam deals with internal emotions and love, Puram focuses on external, public themes like war, valor, and societal duties.
 
• **Prominent Sangam Works:** Key texts include Akananuru*, *Kurunthogai*, and *Narrinai*, which beautifully capture Akam themes.
 
• **Significance:** Sangam literature is an invaluable source for understanding ancient Tamil society, its values, and its poetic traditions.

questions.question: Anti-dumping and anti-subsidies & countervailing measures in India are administered by which Ministry?

__
 
• Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures are administered by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (**DGTR**), which operates under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
• The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) is responsible for investigations and recommendations on anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, and safeguard measures.
 
• Anti-dumping measures are implemented to protect domestic industries from **unfair trade practices** such as dumping, where goods are exported at prices lower than their normal value.
 
• Countervailing measures are aimed at offsetting subsidies provided by the exporting country's government, ensuring fair competition for domestic producers.
 
• The Ministry of Commerce and Industry's role is to ensure compliance with WTO regulations while safeguarding Indian industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Dumping refers to the practice of exporting goods at a price lower than their normal value in the domestic market.
 
• Anti-dumping measures are permitted under the rules of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**.
 
• The goal is to protect domestic industries from material injury caused by unfair pricing.
 
 
 
• **Countervailing Measures:**
 
 
• Countervailing duties are tariffs imposed to counteract subsidies provided by exporting countries to their producers.
 
• These measures ensure a level playing field for domestic industries.
 
 
 
• **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR):**
 
 
• The DGTR was established in 2018 as an integrated authority for administering trade remedy measures.
 
• It consolidates the functions of anti-dumping, countervailing, and safeguard investigations under one body.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO) Compliance:**
 
 
• India's trade remedy measures are aligned with WTO agreements, such as the Agreement on Anti-Dumping and the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was introduced by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 specifically for children?

__
 
• The **86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002** inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This amendment guarantees **free and compulsory education** for children in the specified age group.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE Act) was enacted in **2009** to operationalize Article 21A.
 
• Under the RTE Act, schools are mandated to provide necessary infrastructure, trained teachers, and ensure non-discrimination.

• **Article 21A:** It states that "The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years as determined by law."
 
• **RTE Act, 2009:** This legislation specifies the norms and standards for schools, prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment, and ensures inclusive education for disadvantaged groups.
 
• **Constitutional Significance:** The 86th Amendment also modified **Article 45** (Directive Principles of State Policy) to prioritize early childhood care and education for children below six years.
 
• **Global Context:** India's efforts align with the **United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**, advocating for universal access to education.
 
• **Impact:** The RTE Act and Article 21A have significantly contributed to improving enrollment rates and reducing dropouts, especially among marginalized communities.

questions.question: What is the advantage of keeping food in an airtight container?

options.text: It changes the colour of the food.
It enhances the taste of the food.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It slows down oxidation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Storing food in an airtight container limits the exposure of food to **oxygen**, thereby slowing the process of oxidation.
 
• Oxidation is a chemical reaction where food reacts with oxygen, causing spoilage, changes in texture, taste, and nutritional value.
 
• Airtight containers help in reducing the growth of microorganisms, such as molds and aerobic bacteria, that thrive in the presence of oxygen.
 
• By preventing moisture from entering, airtight containers protect food from becoming stale or soggy.
 
• This method is particularly beneficial for preserving the freshness of dry goods, snacks, and perishable items for longer durations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation Process:**

 
 
• It involves the loss of electrons in food molecules caused by oxygen exposure.
 
• This process leads to rancidity in fats, browning of fruits, and degradation of vitamins.
 
 
 
• **Aerobic vs. Anaerobic Bacteria:**
 
 
• Aerobic bacteria require oxygen to grow, while anaerobic bacteria thrive in oxygen-free environments.
 
• Airtight containers reduce aerobic bacterial growth but do not promote anaerobic bacterial growth unless improperly sealed.
 
 
 
• **Materials Used in Airtight Containers:**
 
 
• Containers are typically made of plastic, glass, or metal with silicone or rubber seals to ensure airtightness.
 
• Proper sealing prevents air and moisture from entering, maintaining food quality.
 
 
 
• **Storage Tips:**
 
 
• Foods with high moisture content should also be kept in airtight containers to avoid mold formation.
 
• Dry goods like grains, cereals, and snacks last longer when stored in airtight conditions.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Techniques:**
 
 
• Airtight storage complements other preservation methods such as refrigeration and freezing.
 
• It is also widely used in vacuum-sealing techniques to extend shelf life.

questions.question: When appointing Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, the President of India acts on the advice of which body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Council of Ministers**__.

__
 
• The President of India appoints Governors of States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories based on the advice of the **Union Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This is in accordance with the principle of the parliamentary system, where the President acts on the advice of the executive body.
 
• The Union Council of Ministers is responsible for aiding and advising the President in exercising their constitutional powers.
 
• Article **74(1)** of the Indian Constitution mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• Governors serve as the constitutional head of the state, and their appointment is a part of the President's discretionary powers, executed in consultation with the executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Council of Ministers:**

 
 
• The Union Council of Ministers comprises the Prime Minister and other ministers, including Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• The Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, as per Article 75 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Role:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state and ensures that the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• They are responsible for summoning and proroguing the state legislature, appointing the Chief Minister, and giving assent to state bills.
 
 
 
• **Lieutenant Governor:**
 
 
• The Lieutenant Governor is the administrative head of Union Territories like Delhi, Puducherry, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• They exercise powers delegated to them by the President of India under various provisions of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 74 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• Mandates that the President shall act in accordance with the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
 
• This ensures that India follows the principles of a parliamentary democracy with a nominal head of state.

questions.question: In MS Word, if you want to duplicate a selected text without removing it from its original location, which set of commands should you use?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Copy → Paste** is used to duplicate a selected text while retaining its original location.
 
• The **Copy** command duplicates the selected text or object and stores it in the clipboard.
 
• The **Paste** command inserts the copied content into a new location specified by the user.
 
• This process allows users to reuse text or objects without modifying or removing the original content.
 
• **Shortcut keys:** Ctrl + C (Copy) and Ctrl + V (Paste) are often used for quick execution of these commands in MS Word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Clipboard:** A temporary storage area in the computer's memory where copied content is saved before it is pasted.
 
• **Cut vs. Copy:** The Cut command removes the content from its original location, while the Copy command duplicates it without removing the original.
 
• **Undo:** If any unwanted action occurs, the Undo command (Ctrl + Z) can reverse the last action performed.
 
• **Move:** This term is often used for relocating content from one place to another, typically using the Cut and Paste commands.
 
• **Drag-and-Drop:** An alternative method to duplicate or move content within MS Word by clicking and dragging the selected text or object.

questions.question: In which year did the English East India Company pass a new law that required every new person who took up employment in the Company’s army to serve overseas if required?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1856**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In **1856**, the English East India Company passed a law mandating that soldiers employed in its army had to serve overseas if required.
 
• This law was significant as it challenged the traditional beliefs of Indian sepoys, particularly regarding crossing the seas, which was considered against their religious practices.
 
• The resentment caused by this law among Indian soldiers contributed to the growing unrest that eventually culminated in the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• This regulation was part of the larger socio-political changes introduced by the British to consolidate their control over India.
 
• The law showcased the disregard of the British towards local cultural sensitivities, leading to widespread dissatisfaction among Indian troops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• The revolt was triggered by multiple factors, including resentment over policies like the overseas service law and the introduction of Enfield rifles with cartridges rumored to be greased with cow and pig fat.
 
• It is considered the first major uprising against British rule in India.
 
• Both sepoys and civilians participated in the revolt, which started in Meerut and spread across northern and central India.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Sensitivities:**
 
 
• Crossing the seas was considered a religious taboo among certain Indian communities, as it was believed to result in the loss of caste.
 
• The imposition of the overseas service regulation was seen as an affront to traditional values.
 
 
 
• **English East India Company:**
 
 
• The company governed India until 1858, after which control was transferred to the British Crown.
 
• Its policies often ignored local customs, leading to widespread dissatisfaction and resistance among Indians.
 
 
 
• **Military Reforms:**
 
 
• British reforms in the Indian army aimed at aligning the forces with Western military practices.
 
• These reforms were often resisted by Indian soldiers due to cultural and religious differences.
